title: Audit shipper: signed-upload and streaming modes for customer-managed storage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a robust audit-shipper that can forward audit logs from Private/VPC/on-prem deployments into customer-managed object storage (S3/GCS/Blob). Provide two transport modes: (1) presigned/signed-upload flow where the shipper issues short-lived upload credentials/URLs to an internal relay that writes directly to customer buckets, and (2) encrypted server-to-storage streaming for environments that disallow external direct uploads. Ensure KMS-wrapping for metadata, support retention lifecycle headers, and produce observable delivery guarantees and idempotency for retries.
acceptance_criteria: Ship logs successfully to S3/GCS/Azure Blob using presigned PUT with TTL <= 5m
Support server-side streaming mode that sends encrypted chunks over an outbound allowed port and performs multipart commit to target storage
Integrations with customer KMS for metadata envelope encryption and optional SSE-C / SSE-KMS workflow documented
End-to-end tests exercising retry semantics, duplicate suppression, and manifest reconciliation
Security review completed and threat-model mitigations documented
implementation_notes: Provide two modes selectable per-deployment: 'presigned' and 'streaming'

Presigned mode: shipper requests a scoped signed URL token from control plane (or customer-supplied signer) and returns it to onprem relay; the relay performs eventual PUTs and posts metadata back to shipper

Streaming mode: shipper maintains an outbound TLS connection to customer endpoint or directly to cloud storage gateway; use chunked, signed multipart uploads with per-chunk sequence numbers for idempotency
All payloads MUST be SHA256-signed and accompanied by audit-manifest JSON describing sequence, compression, and compression-checksum
Use envelope encryption: log payload encrypted with ephemeral data key; data key wrapped by customer KMS (CMK) and stored alongside manifest
Retention: set lifecycle headers and object tags where supported; for GCS use retentionPolicy metadata and hold flags
Fallback: if presigned uploads fail due to firewall, automatically switch to streaming mode if policy permits
Expose metrics: upload_latency_ms, upload_retries, bytes_forwarded, last_success_timestamp, manifest_lag_seconds
decisions: Prefer customer-managed KMS wrapping (CMK) over Redwood-managed keys when CMK is configured to minimize trust surface
Do not keep plaintext copies of logs on control-plane; shipper will only store encrypted manifests and short-lived telemetry
Presigned URLs limited to PUT object with sized Content-Length to prevent partial uploads and SMP abuse
Signed upload TTL chosen as 5 minutes by default (trade-off between security and operational failures behind NAT)
risks: Customer firewall policies may block presigned uploads; must provide streaming fallback and clear operational runbook
KMS throttling could cause shipper stalls — add exponential backoff with scheduled background retries
Large backlog spikes could exhaust local disk; need configurable local buffering + eviction policy and alerting
Misconfigured retention/lifecycle tags could lead to non-compliant retention; include reconciliation job to verify object retention settings
testing_plan: Integration tests using localstack (S3) + test GCS emulator exercising presigned and streaming flows
Chaos test: drop randomized outbound packets and verify retry and idempotent behavior
Security tests: attempt replay of old signed URLs, attempt tampering with manifests, validate signature enforcement
Performance tests: sustained 1 MB/s per instance for 1 hour, validate latency and resource usage
E2E runbook verification with sample customer environment (staging VPC)
